newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel labour federation sells Hapoalim stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel labour federation sells Hapoalim stake.

text.p: Israel's Histadrut labour federation signed an agreement on Wednesday for the sale of its three percent stake in Bank Hapoalim to a U.S. investor group.
Shmuel Avital, head of the Histadrut's finance and economics division, said the price was 168 million shekels ($52 million).
The investor group is led by Jeffrey Keil, who recently left his job as president of Republic New York Corp to form an investment partnership.

Avital said the Histadrut, which began negotiations two months ago with a number of potential buyers, decided to sell its remaining stake in Israel's largest bank to pay off a 150 million shekel loan.
About 20 percent of Hapoalim is traded on the Tel Aviv stock exchange. The rest of its stock is owned by the government.
According to senior Treasury officials, Keil has expressed interest in buying a controlling stake in Hapoalim from the government.

Keil reportedly has joined a group of investors headed by Israeli businessman Eliezer Fishman who are bidding for a controlling interest in Hapoalim. The group includes U.S. based Reliance Insurance and Bear Stearns.

The Fishman group is the only bidder for the Hapoalim stake. A group headed by Claridge Israel, the investment arm of Canadian billionaire Charles Bronfman, announced in August that it was no longer interested in purchasing the controlling stake.
